extracted.intended_audience: general readers, book buyers, and writers interested in literary qualities
extracted.subtask_description: Extract evaluative criteria for creative writing from short book blurbs and publisher descriptions; these blurbs identify qualities (voice, vividness, economy, etc.) that mark strong literary work. Use those phrased criteria as guidance for assessing or producing literary prose and fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: poetic vision and intimate knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: 'a man of poetic vision, with an intimate knowledge of particular conditions of life, here looks out upon a world...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing should combine a distinctive poetic sensibility with close, informed observation of particular social or physical conditions; the author's vision elevates ordinary reality. Example: narrative voice that perceives and renders subtle social detail without losing lyric quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: vividness and vivacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Described as 'vivid, vivacious, scintillating.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prose and scenes should feel lively and visually striking; energetic diction and dynamic imagery sustain reader interest. Used to praise portrayals of place and life whose depiction sparkles and feels immediate.

rubrics_metrics.name: range of subject balanced with focused perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: 'These stories have considerable range of subject, but in general they are stay-at-home tales depicting cloistered lives and delicate, finely fibred minds.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work may cover a wide set of topics yet retain a coherent focus or thematic concentration (e.g., domestic life). Balance breadth of subject with consistent tonal/psychological perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: economy of language / never wastes a word
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Bierce never wastes a word.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concise, tightly controlled prose is valued; economy helps build impact and final effects. Avoid unnecessary ornamentation; each word should contribute to meaning or effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: subtle realism producing emotional effect
rubrics_metrics.description: 'simple, yet subtle, realism. He secures his final effect, a cold thrill of fear, by a simple, yet subtle, realism.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Realism need not be heavy-handed; truthful, understated depiction can generate strong emotional responses. Use restrained detail and implication to evoke mood (e.g., dread, suspense).

rubrics_metrics.name: serenity in presenting strong feeling and audacious thought
rubrics_metrics.description: 'It is characteristic of Jane Austen’s art that she presents this story, which was the fruit of strong feeling and audacious thought, with such perfect serenity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Powerful themes or bold ideas are made more effective when presented with composure—calm tone allows complexity to register without melodrama. Control of tone fosters reader acceptance of striking material.

rubrics_metrics.name: timelessness / universal appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: 'You may read this grim story ... at any age and come under its sway.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that speaks across ages and contexts—with universal emotional or thematic reach—is singled out as great. Aim for specific detail that also resonates with broad human concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: showing rather than telling; implication
rubrics_metrics.description: 'He shows nothing, and yet everything.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on implication, selective detail, and scenes to suggest larger realities; avoid explicit exposition when indirect presentation will produce richer effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: poetical order and reflective detachment
rubrics_metrics.description: 'A novel of rare poetical order ... while identified with his creations ... the author has known how to detach himself from these figures ... and show them, with all their tumultuous, passionate emotions, in a beautiful mirror.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine lyric or structured artistry ('poetical order') with authorial control (detachment) that lets characters stand free for reflection. Balance empathy with critical distance to provide clarity of depiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: pungency and wit
rubrics_metrics.description: 'In these essays Mr. Belloc attains his usual high level of pungent and witty writing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sharpness of phrase and wit enliven essays and short pieces; pungency implies concentrated, piquant observation or aphoristic remark. Use economy plus wit to deliver memorable lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: vivid immediacy from the opening pages
rubrics_metrics.description: 'It is vivid from the first page to the last.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustained vividness that begins immediately draws readers in; openings should establish tone, scene, or voice strongly so momentum carries through the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: faithful rendering of everyday life / use of memory
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The life-story ... in which the author draws on his memory for a picture of the everyday life of his immediate forbears.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authenticity in depicting quotidian experience—often drawn from memory—lends credibility and texture. Concrete, lived detail builds verisimilitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: craftsmanship, completeness, and enduring quality
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Something worth doing and done ... destined to endure, and ... a success.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-made works show care in execution and cohesion; craftsmanship includes polished plotting, language, and structure that suggest lasting value.

rubrics_metrics.name: absorbing narrative and narrative authority
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Here is a history which is more absorbing than any work of fiction.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A narrative (fiction or non-fiction) that engrosses the reader—through storytelling skill and authoritative voice—can transcend genre. Control of pace, selection, and emphasis maintains absorption.

rubrics_metrics.name: satire as social critique: wit, malice, and coolness
rubrics_metrics.description: 'He waged a sleepless war with the mental torpor of the prosperous ... a Swift with the soul of music in him, and completely sane; a liberator of humanity operating with the wit and malice and coolness of Mephistopheles.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective satire combines moral purpose with stylistic mastery: sharp wit, biting judgment, and a composed delivery. Satire should expose complacency and provoke thought without collapsing into mere invective.

rubrics_metrics.name: inobtrusive workmanship
rubrics_metrics.description: 'It is because of the inobtrusiveness of this workmanship, that for once the critic and the reader may join hands without awaiting the verdict of posterity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skill should not draw attention to itself; art that seems effortless and unobtrusive often succeeds best. Seamless technique lets story and character remain central.

rubrics_metrics.name: sensory detail and gaudy presence
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Mr. Duguid’s prose admirably renders the brute, physical aspect of the scene so that it seems present in all its overpowering gaudiness to the senses.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rich sensory description (color, texture, sound, smell) can make scenes physically immediate; be vivid but balanced to avoid purple prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: attention to specific local detail and factual knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: 'His knowledge of the English countryside is extraordinary; he can not only name the trees and flowers, the birds and beasts of every district, but he can tell what every village is built of and why.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific, reportable detail grounds fiction/travel writing; demonstrable knowledge of place and custom increases authenticity and reader trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: use of a central event to reveal communal life
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Through the medium of a cricket match the author endeavours to give a glimpse of life in a Sussex village.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing a narrative around a single event can serve as a microcosm revealing wider social relationships and character dynamics; structure vignettes to let an event illuminate community.

rubrics_metrics.name: concentration, disciplined study, and orderliness
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Concentration, "never reading but always studying," dismissing trivialities and only reading masterpieces, orderliness, taking notes, avoiding laziness — it is with such aids to improving the mind that M. Dimnet chiefly deals.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creative and critical practice benefits from focused study habits: selectivity in reading, systematic note-taking, and disciplined work improve thinking and craft. This is prescriptive guidance for writers and thinkers.

rubrics_metrics.name: blend of personal experience with historical context
rubrics_metrics.description: '...deals with places shaken by the heavy footsteps of History. Underneath, the book is an ode to railroad travel.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective travel or historical writing links subjective experience to broader historical forces, providing both personal immediacy and contextual significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: character growth and inner transformation
rubrics_metrics.description: '...first awake in the heroine the historic imagination ... she grows all at once into a powerful and wilful young creature, gets her courage, and begins to find herself.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compelling fiction often charts internal development: believable stages of maturation or change anchored in events and sensory detail create satisfying arcs.

rubrics_metrics.name: modern impressions, delicate perception, and expressive gift
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Very modern in impressions, in appreciations, in curiosities, and in his very love of the mother earth ... with delicate perceptions and a gift for expression ... captured for us the spirit of modern travel itself.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A contemporary sensibility—attuned observation and an expressive style—can capture the spirit of an age or genre (e.g., modern travel). Combine fresh observations with controlled expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: readability and sustained engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: 'A book which is readable from the first page to the last.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity, pacing, and compelling material keep readers engaged throughout. Prioritize momentum, clear prose, and scenecraft to maintain readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: clarity and firmness of artistic principle
rubrics_metrics.description: 'It remains perpetually the novel of all novels which the criticism of fiction cannot overlook; ... the subject stands firm and clear, without the least shade of ambiguity to break the line which bounds it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong work often has a clear central subject or organizing principle; clarity of intent and restraint from unnecessary ambiguity help the work cohere conceptually and thematically.

rubrics_metrics.name: musicality and exactness of prose
rubrics_metrics.description: 'his prose is exact and clean and full of music.' 'clear, musical prose.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attention to sentence rhythm, sound, and precise diction enhances pleasure and memorability. Strive for linguistic exactness combined with musical cadence.
